assumptions: Ball centers are unrestricted points in R^2.
claim: Four-point radius witnesses are sufficient for planar sign-quotient ball feasibility.
possible_failure_mode: Five approximately equally spaced projective directions may require a larger covering radius collectively than every four-point subset. The proposed witness fails if an unrestricted center and alternative sign lift cover all five within radius 9/10.
research_question: Does the failure of three-point completeness extend to four-point completeness in the planar sign quotient?
stop_condition: Stop after exact verification of this five-point candidate; accept a counterexample only if every subset of size at most four is feasible and the full set is infeasible.
verification_plan: Enumerate sign lifts and compute exact smallest enclosing ball radii for the five-point set and its four-point subsets.
Compare squared radii with 81/100 using exact arithmetic.
Use containment to infer feasibility of smaller subsets from feasibility of all four-point subsets.
why_this_matters: A verified counterexample would raise the necessary universal witness size to at least five, materially strengthening the existing failure of three-point completeness and constraining replacement witness theorems.
